title: 75% of Employees Lose Focus During Online Meetings
paragraphs: It can be hard to focus during any meeting — and with so many digital distractions right there on our screens, it can be even harder to focus during an online meeting!
In fact, a survey has found that three in four employees admit to losing focus during online meetings.
Australian recruitment company People2people surveyed over 1,200 workers about online meetings.
Just 8% said they always give online meetings their full attention, while 75% said they lose full focus in most online meetings — or in all of them!
So why are workers losing focus?

Almost a third of participants said they find it difficult to pay attention if the meeting goes on for too long, while almost a quarter said it's because they have too many meetings. And 39% said they lose focus if the meeting is not relevant to them.
However, while some may not be paying attention to what's being said in the meeting, they might be paying attention to what their colleagues are doing!
Sixty-one percent said that, in a typical online meeting, it seems as though at least half of the people are multitasking.
Many participants said they browse online instead of listening to what's being said in a meeting, and 32% said they work on other tasks. A few people also said they check their messages.

People2people said this multitasking is a problem, because it might mean information is missed, conversations have to be repeated, decisions are slower, and employees leave meetings without a clear understanding of what was agreed.

The company said employers can address this problem by having shorter meetings with clear agendas and fewer people. They could also make better use of written updates, to make sure important information is received.
